<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_references.py; edit specs/dasdae-inventory.yml instead. -->

Measured control-point map from an acquisition's channel-like coordinate onto optical path distance.

::: {.note}
A channel map is a function, not a roster. It answers where a channel would fall on the optical path; it does not list which channels exist. Values between control points are resolved by piecewise linear interpolation, and channels outside the covered range are undefined. Exactly one input axis is populated — channel when the interrogator reports channel numbers, instrument_distance when it reports its own nominal meters. A single-point map takes its interpolation slope from the acquisition's nominal spatial_interval.
:::

Aliases: `DistMap`, `Distance map`

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | tuple[float, ...] \| None | Interrogator-reported channel numbers at the control points; strictly increasing. |
| `instrument_distance` | tuple[float, ...] \| None | Interrogator-reported nominal distances at the control points in meters; strictly increasing. |
| `distance` | tuple[float, ...] | Optical path distances at the control points in meters; strictly increasing. |
